**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-10 17:58 UTC

Yeah, this has been failing for some time nondeterministically. I haven't been able to reproduce locally; options include just deleting the test and replacing it with some other way to test what we want to test, adding print-debugging for what exactly is in the `zerver_client` table and what object it got out of a cache that is different, etc.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-10 17:59 UTC

I'm pretty sure it is an issue where we got a value for a `client` object out of a cache that had been created (and deleted) in a previous test and somehow escaped our various mechanisms in `test_runner.py` and `test_classes.py` for clearing/invalidating caches between tests.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-10 17:59 UTC

I guess the most likely story since this is a Tornado thing is that we have a stale `ClientDescriptor` object created in a previous test, since those things are probably not garbage-collected?

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-10-11 13:37 UTC

I looked into it today

The test is to verify that we don't send email/push notifications via `missedmessage_hook` codepath when the `disable_external_notification` parameter is true while sending a message. e.g. welcome_bot.

This function returns cached result.
```
@cache_with_key(get_client_cache_key, timeout=3600 * 24 * 7)
def get_client_remote_cache(name: str) -> Client:
    (client, _) = Client.objects.get_or_create(name=name[0 : Client.MAX_NAME_LENGTH])
    return client
```

Also, the [error log shows](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/actions/runs/6442021073/job/17492406447?pr=27110#step:19:4628) the error at:
```
self._post_teardown()
self._fixture_teardown()
```

I looked into `django.test.testcase`
For `SimpleTestCase` the [`_post_teardown()`](https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/test/testcases.py#L311) is just `pass`

But the error we have is for [`_post_teardown()`](https://github.com/django/django/blob/main/django/test/testcases.py#L1104) in `TransactionTestCase` which is a bit confusing,

In summary, we didn't find the perfect fix as it is kind of difficult to verify locally, but I got some insights today, so I'm hopeful to fix it soon.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-11 20:28 UTC

@Zixuan James Li FYI in case you have an idea for how `TransactionTestCase` might be involved here.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-11 20:30 UTC

In theory, `bounce_key_prefix_for_testing` should change the `KEY_PREFIX` for all our caches at the start of each test.

**Tim Abbott** · 2023-10-11 20:30 UTC

Defined in `ZulipTestCaseMixin.set_up`

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-10-11 20:43 UTC

The remaining part of the call stack shouldn't be there for `ZulipTransactionTestCase`, because we have overriden it to be empty.

**Zixuan James Li** · 2023-10-11 20:49 UTC

`TestCase` is a subclass of `TransactionTestCase`, and the error happens in [`_fixture_teardown`](https://github.com/django/django/blob/8adc7c86ab85ed91e512bc49056e301cbe1715d0/django/test/testcases.py#L1328-L1336) of `TestCase`.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2023-10-12 13:55 UTC

Okay, we don't have `super().setUp()` and `super().tearDown()` in `setUp(self)` and `tearDown(self)` of `MissedMessageHookTest` which would be resulting in cached `zerver_client` being used. Hence the error:

> DETAIL:  Key (sending_client_id)=(116) is not present in table "zerver_client".

```

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2024-06-20 19:46 UTC

Don’t use `&nbsp;`. Firstly, we don’t want to prevent these lists from wrapping, and secondly, `&nbsp;` really does render to a different Unicode character that’s not equal to a space character. A regular space character works fine in `{{#unless @last}}, {{/unless}}`. The Handlebars whitespace control in `{{~/each}}` only suppresses the previous run of consecutive whitespace *in the Handlebars source*, and does not cross past directives or anything else ([documentation](https://handlebarsjs.com/guide/expressions.html#whitespace-control)).

**Apoorva Pendse** · 2024-11-07 08:10 UTC

Went through it, it was my own fault.

I made a breaking change inside bootstrap_typeahead.ts which the code playground used to give language selection typeaheads.

Added this if condition to trigger lookup() for topics after stream is selected just to "make it work" for the compose typeahead.

This ended up never closing the typeahead menu in case of the playground typeahead for languages, therefore causing the selection of wrong option.

The key was to alter the function definition for hideAfterSelect() function which has a default implementation of return true, closing the typeahead after something is selected.

I changed it so that it didn't close the typeahead only when the stream is being completed

The puppeteer test for realm playground does pass now (locally).
Hope it does on the CI as well

## python-zulip-api failing CI on Py3.8 zulip3.2

*2024-11-14 to 2024-11-14 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/43-automated-testing/topic/python-zulip-api.20failing.20CI.20on.20Py3.2E8.20zulip3.2E2/with/1981167)*

**Niloth** · 2024-11-14 11:19 UTC

I was looking into the [failing CI](https://github.com/zulip/python-zulip-api/actions/runs/11601363279/job/32303908627) , and here's what I gathered.

In `zulip 3.2`, `Twisted` is listed as an explicit dependency, and it has `Incremental` as a dependency.

Bugs (clashes with setuptools behavior) have been reported on Incremental's latest versions - [24.7.0](https://github.com/twisted/incremental/issues/100#issuecomment-2253267576), [24.7.1](https://github.com/twisted/incremental/issues/106), and they were [fixed](https://github.com/twisted/incremental/pull/107) shortly after. But, they've listed [`setuptools>=61.0`](https://github.com/twisted/incremental/blob/trunk/pyproject.toml#L4) as a requirement, and we're using `setuptools==49.1.0`, so I'm not sure if we can raise an issue there asking for a resolution.

**Niloth** · 2024-11-14 11:20 UTC

If we could pin `twisted<=22.10.0`, which then automatically pins down `incremental<=22.10.0`, the setuptools conflict would also be resolved (tested locally), but we can't backport to `3.2`.

**Niloth** · 2024-11-14 11:20 UTC

What's the general approach in this situation?
Can we be raising an issue even if our `setuptools` is below the required version? Should we ourselves attempt raising a PR that patches this?

**Tim Abbott** · 2024-11-14 17:10 UTC

Why do we depend on twisted? I'm not sure it's a library we use directly.

**Neil Pilgrim (neiljp)** · 2024-11-14 17:19 UTC

I find `pipdeptree` useful here, if you've not tried it.

```spoiler Code from your PR
```python
def find_js_test_files(test_dir: str, files: Iterable[str]) -> list[str]:
    """
    Find test files in the test directory with improved matching and error handling.
    Supports both direct matches and partial names, with special handling for test files.

    Args:
        test_dir: Directory containing test files
        files: Iterable of file names or patterns to match

    Returns:
        list[str]: List of absolute paths to matching test files

    Raises:
        Exception: If no matching test files are found with helpful suggestion message
    """
    test_files: list[str] = []
    available_files = os.listdir(test_dir)

    for file in files:
        # Remove extension if provided
        base_name, ext = os.path.splitext(file)

        # Check if a valid test file exists
        matches = [
            f
            for f in available_files
            if f.startswith(base_name) and f.endswith((".test.ts", ".test.js"))
        ]

        # Raise an error if a file exists but is not a valid test file
        if not matches:
            similar_files = [
                f
                for f in available_files
                if f.startswith(base_name) or f.endswith((".test.ts", ".test.js"))
            ]

            if f"{base_name}.ts" in similar_files or f"{base_name}.js" in similar_files:
                raise Exception(
                    f"'{file}' is not a valid test file. Test files must end with '.test.ts' or '.test.js'"
                )

            error_msg = f"Cannot find a matching test file for '{file}' in '{test_dir}'"
            if similar_files:
                error_msg += "\nDid you mean one of these?\n" + "\n".join(
                    f"- {f}" for f in similar_files if f.endswith((".test.ts", ".test.js"))
                )
            raise Exception(error_msg)

        # Add absolute path of matching file
        test_files.extend(os.path.abspath(os.path.join(test_dir, match)) for match in matches)

    # If no specific files were passed, return all test files in the directory
    if not files:
        test_files = sorted(
            glob.glob(os.path.join(test_dir, "*.test.ts"))
            + glob.glob(os.path.join(test_dir, "*.test.js"))
        )

    return test_files

    """
    Find test files in the test directory with improved matching and error handling.
    Supports both direct matches and partial names, with special handling for test files.

    Args:
        test_dir: Directory containing test files
        files: Iterable of file names or patterns to match

    Returns:
        list[str]: List of absolute paths to matching test files

    Raises:
        Exception: If no matching test files are found with helpful suggestion message
    """
    test_files: list[str] = []
    available_files = os.listdir(test_dir)

    for file in files:
        # Remove extension if provided
        base_name = os.path.splitext(file)[0]

        # Find all possible matches
        matches = [
            f
            for f in available_files
            if f.startswith(base_name) and f.endswith((".test.ts", ".test.js"))
        ]

        # If no test file matches found, look for similar files for error message
        if not matches:
            similar_files = [
                f
                for f in available_files
                if f.startswith(base_name) or f.endswith((".test.ts", ".test.js"))
            ]

            error_msg = f"Cannot find a matching test file for '{file}' in '{test_dir}'"
            if similar_files:
                error_msg += "\nDid you mean one of these?\n" + "\n".join(
                    f"- {f}" for f in similar_files if f.endswith((".test.ts", ".test.js"))
                )
                if any(f == base_name + ".ts" or f == base_name + ".js" for f in similar_files):
                    error_msg += f"\n\nNote: '{base_name}.ts' is not a test file. Test files should end with '.test.ts'"
            raise Exception(error_msg)

        # Add absolute path of matching file
        test_files.extend(os.path.abspath(os.path.join(test_dir, match)) for match in matches)

    # If no files specified, return all test files
    if not test_files:
        test_files = sorted(
            glob.glob(os.path.join(test_dir, "*.test.ts"))
            + glob.glob(os.path.join(test_dir, "*.test.js"))
        )

    return test_files
```

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-01-14 15:58 UTC

> So just send the event with the more simple `send_event` API.

`send_event_rollback_unsafe` does the same thing which you're suggesting.

We have `send_event_on_commit` for "send event only when transaction commits".

```py
def send_event_on_commit(
    realm: Realm, event: Mapping[str, Any], users: Iterable[int] | Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]]
) -> None:
    transaction.on_commit(lambda: send_event_rollback_unsafe(realm, event, users))
```

## assertCountEqual

*2025-01-22 to 2025-01-22 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/43-automated-testing/topic/assertCountEqual/with/2053215)*

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-22 02:21 UTC

We have several uses of `assertCountEqual` in our test code.  It's a very strange name that the `unittest` modules uses, because it sounds like you are comparing the counts of two sequences.  It's actually more like `assertSameSetOfValues`, because it actually checks that the sequences have the same values (and same count of values), but possibly in a different order.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-22 02:23 UTC

I feel like it's almost always a code smell when using this that we aren't just properly using a set in the real code. I guess one nuance is that you could be comparing two different sequences that both duplicate an element the same number of times, but that's smelly in its own way.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-22 02:26 UTC

An example is `get_slim_realm_default_streams`, which currently returns a list, but there's no reason for it to not return a set, since the query it uses has no ordering anyway.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-22 02:27 UTC

And then instead of this:

~~~ py
 982         default_streams = get_slim_realm_default_streams(realm.id)
 983         self.assert_length(default_streams, 3)
 984         self.assertCountEqual(default_streams, [verona, sandbox, zulip])
~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-22 02:28 UTC

We could just do this, correct?

~~~ py
 982         default_streams = get_slim_realm_default_streams(realm.id)
 983         self.assertEqual(default_streams, {verona, sandbox, zulip})

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-22 02:31 UTC

~~Hrm, maybe in this example, the objects support equality checks but aren't hashable into sets?~~

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-22 03:02 UTC

#33134 addresses the above

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-22 18:53 UTC

Yeah I think comparing sets is going to be more intuitive most of the time. The logical behavior is different if there's multiple copies of the same value in a list, but that's likely not the scenario in any Zulip tests.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-01-22 18:55 UTC

Merged #33134.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-01-22 19:06 UTC

## unusual `.message_inline_image` HTML

*2025-09-17 to 2025-09-17 · 20 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/43-automated-testing/topic/unusual.20.60.2Emessage_inline_image.60.20HTML/with/2261064)*

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 14:22 UTC

While revising #36052, which does a client-side rewrite of the `.message_inline_image` class used on the server, I noticed for the first time this unusual bit of HTML that gets handed over for postprocessing in the `postprocess_content.test.cjs` file (here pulled out of the concatenated strings in the test file as just an HTML block):

```html
<div class="message_inline_image">
  <a href="http://zulip.zulipdev.com/user_uploads/w/ha/tever/inline.png" title="inline image">upload</a>
  <a role="button">button</a>
</div>
```

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 14:24 UTC

After post-processing, the contents of the block remain unchanged. And I can find nothing obvious server-side that introduces something like the `<a role="button">button</a>` component.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 14:25 UTC

The biggest issue here is that, according to the tests and the logic I'd written previously, such blocks should be placed inside image galleries. That seems incorrect here, as again the inner HTML remains unchanged, so there's no `<img>` tag that we can render.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 14:26 UTC

I'm curious whether anyone can shed some light on where that test case came from, and if there's some way to actually replicate that in Zulip in the dev environment.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 14:28 UTC

Looks like the germ of this line was introduced in 3df0cacd9e1e43ec5bcdbf60938a3174798e63cb, and not that long ago (March of 2022)

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 14:31 UTC

And then the `<a role="button">` part was introduced sometime a few months later, as part of some Typescript work: 911b3b5365d9bfd935b04b5406bb302616c02783

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 14:34 UTC

One can get a similar but not identical pattern by linking to an external image with custom text, but that a) produces no weird `<a role="button">` element, and is processed to present the image as an `<img>` tag, which does not match the pattern suggested in the test.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-09-17 15:18 UTC

Given that you posted in #**automated testing**, I wonder if your hunch here is that the existing tests were somewhat contrived.  Are your substantive changes possibly just revealing that the original tests weren't really testing real-world behavior?

I don't have any insight on the recent commits.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 15:25 UTC

I think that's likely the case. I've removed the tests to see what coverage complains, and it seems like the tests in question could indeed be contrived and meant to simply satisfy test coverage. 

I'm looking to add a new test example that will satisfy coverage while not being contrived, but it seems like just adding an `href`-less `<a>` will suffice (and which one can arrive at via `[some missing link]()`--making it a non-contrived case). 

Other bits of coverage, including the `title`/`aria-label` bits introduced in 3df0cacd9e1e43ec5bcdbf60938a3174798e63cb are already handled in non-contrived examples.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-09-17 15:29 UTC

I think it's always a good idea to replace a cryptic test with a more clear test.  Our tests are often far from perfect.  It seems like you have done enough due diligence to be sure that removing the test doesn't introduce a regression.   Having said that, I would try to drill down on which particular commit breaks the test and give it a little extra scrutiny.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-09-17 15:30 UTC

If nothing else, I think it would be good to retire the broken test in the commit that actually exposes its brokenness.  (if you haven't done so already)

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 15:34 UTC

I have. I also want to reread the server-side processing logic (along with its tests) that introduces `.message_inline_image` to further verify that there aren’t any cases where we use that class on an ordinary link that doesn’t get processed further to include an `<img>` or `<video>` element to the linked resource in question.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-09-17 15:39 UTC

Can you excerpt the test in question?  I think it would be helpful to explain on a high level what the post-processing logic is intended to do.  It's interesting that the test in question is JS-side but you also mention server-side processing logic.

The one benefit of a smelly test, as I'm sure you're aware of, is that despite its painfulness and possibly awkwardly-written legacy is that it might reveal some crufty-ness in the actual code.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 15:45 UTC

I can't excerpt it easily, no...which is why I isolated the problem chunk the way I did [above](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/43-automated-testing/topic/unusual.20.60.2Emessage_inline_image.60.20HTML/near/2261064). As you can quickly see on GitHub, we have [a huge catchall `postprocess_content` test](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/main/web/tests/postprocess_content.test.cjs) beginning near line 16. That corresponds, for good or ill, to [the massive `for` loop in `postprocess_content.ts`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/main/web/src/postprocess_content.ts) beginning near line 15 in that file.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 15:45 UTC

As with the `for` loop, the common denominator with that lump of tests is the presence of `<a>` elements in some shape or form.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 15:50 UTC

It seems like at the very least we could split that up into processing links that have nothing to do with media elements, and then a separate test for those that do. What we're basically doing in that test is imagining a very complex, edge-case-loaded message and testing its post-processed output.

What I discovered yesterday and what prompted this thread is that the presence of the contrived example reveals that *order* matters here in ways that are troubling--presently, we're pretending the contrived example can be tucked inside an image gallery, but because the contrived example is, um, contrived, that wouldn't ever (or shouldn't ever) actually happen. But in my efforts to clean up and de-obfuscate how we process genuine inline media with the `.message_inline_image` class, this case revealed itself.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 15:53 UTC

Most notably, doing a simple wholesale client-side switcheroo from `.message_inline_image` to my original proposed `.message-linked-media` left this test quietly happy. But in doing as Tim suggested in #**frontend>renaming .message_inline_image class**, in processing two separate classes depending on the presence of an `<img>` or a `<video>` element, which is handled server-side, I discovered that we have these few lines of test case that do not seem like something the server is actually capable of coughing up.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 16:34 UTC

(replying to Karl Stolley)
> It seems like at the very least we could split that up into processing links that have nothing to do with media elements

Indeed this is how this particular test used to look. [Back when it was part of a `util.js` test file](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/911b3b5365d9bfd935b04b5406bb302616c02783/frontend_tests/node_tests/util.js#L257), the test was specific to cleaning up user links. At some point (I haven't reviewed when), that test moved into `postprocess_content.test.cjs`, and over time has grown to include cases that involve run-of-the-mill processing, rather than just link cleanup.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-09-17 19:28 UTC

The first two commits to #36052 now include the changes I proposed here.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-09-17 20:07 UTC

Yeah those buttons aren't real, this is a buggy test.

In general, the HTML for those tests should probably be coming from `markdown_test_cases.json` or https://zulip.com/api/message-formatting, with a reference comment, and any exceptions to that should have a comment. (oembed is a possible source of weird exceptions)

@@ -5704,3 +5704,5 @@ def customer_has_last_n_invoices_open(customer: Customer, n: int) -> bool:

+    )
     for customer in customers:

## unknown CSS properties discarded in unit tests

*2026-04-20 to 2026-04-27 · 20 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/43-automated-testing/topic/unknown.20CSS.20properties.20discarded.20in.20unit.20tests/with/2439149)*

**Karl Stolley** · 2026-04-20 17:13 UTC

I've got a draft PR up, #39034, which uses the browser-native `<element>.style.setProperty` to set a value on the CSS `aspect-ratio` property. That change *should* be breaking a whole bunch of tests in ``web/tests/postprocess_content.test.cjs`, but it's not--as it appears the test suite discards CSS properties that it doesn't know.

**Karl Stolley** · 2026-04-20 17:14 UTC

While we have mocked a bunch of jQuery-based manipulations in the `zquery` library, I'm uncertain about how to do something similar so that `aspect-ratio` is recognized when set with native browser methods for doing so.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-04-20 17:52 UTC

I would consider asking Claude Code to handle it -- I've been quite happy with its work on the node test libraries.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2026-04-21 03:20 UTC

I’m pretty sure there’s no jQuery nor zjquery involved in that test. It’s all JSDOM.

**Karl Stolley** · 2026-04-21 13:30 UTC

That’s correct. It’s all native browser methods there, which I’d like to know how to properly extend if possible.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2026-04-21 20:14 UTC

Try to figure out in what way JSDOM doesn’t match the browser, minimize a test case, and open an upstream issue or pull request with JSDOM.

**Karl Stolley** · 2026-04-21 20:16 UTC

Got it. What I'm seeing is that it's discarding CSS properties it doesn't know about, so I wouldn't be surprised if that's an upstream dependency. But I'll definitely take the approach you suggest, Anders. Thanks!

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2026-04-21 20:17 UTC

Probably related: https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom/issues/2089

**Karl Stolley** · 2026-04-21 20:18 UTC

Almost certainly

**Dhruv Vira** · 2026-04-23 17:48 UTC

@Karl Stolley, I'd love to help out here. I can look into creating a minimal reproduction case for the JSDOM upstream issue. I can also look into how we can mock such properties like `aspect-ratio` so that the node test does not discard it.
Let me know if I can be of any help.

**Karl Stolley** · 2026-04-23 17:49 UTC

You're welcome to investigate

**Dhruv Vira** · 2026-04-23 20:17 UTC

Got to the bottom of this.
This issue isn't that JSDOM discards the `aspect-ratio`. It's just that it expects "width / height" format and when we do not provide it the aspect ratio in that format, it discards the style.
In #39034, `${original_width / original_height}` was being passed as the aspect ratio. It means if the aspect ratio was 16/9, 1.7777 was being passed as the property value. Since JSDOM specifically wants aspect ratio value in "16/9" format, when it receives the decimal 1.7777, it discards the style.

We can see that exact behavior here:
1.
```
el.style.setProperty("aspect-ratio", "16 / 9");
console.log("With Slash:  ", el.outerHTML);
```
gives output: `With Slash:   <div id="my-div" style="aspect-ratio: 16 / 9;"></div>`

2.
```
el.style.setProperty("aspect-ratio", "1.7777");
console.log("With Decimal:", el.outerHTML);
```
gives output: `With Decimal: <div id="my-div" style=""></div>`

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2026-04-23 20:21 UTC

Cool. We should report that upstream, since `1.7777` is a [valid value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing-4/#aspect-ratio) that should be accepted.

**Karl Stolley** · 2026-04-23 20:21 UTC

Oh, that’s some nice detective work!

**Dhruv Vira** · 2026-04-23 20:42 UTC

(replying to Anders Kaseorg)
> Cool. We should report that upstream, since `1.7777` is a [valid value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing-4/#aspect-ratio) that should be accepted.

I'd love to take care of it, if that's fine.

**Dhruv Vira** · 2026-04-23 20:42 UTC

#39087 fixes our node test.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2026-04-23 20:43 UTC

Given that we already set `width` and `height`, does `aspect-ratio: auto` not accomplish the same goal here?

**Karl Stolley** · 2026-04-23 20:45 UTC

It doesn’t, regrettably. I have found that flexbox still collapses replaced content until it’s loaded, causing the layout shifts we’re trying to avoid
